title: G3 Candidate Enumerator
objective: Make exact genus-3 Weil-candidate enumeration fast while preserving exact Sturm semantics and ordinary Python fallback

handoff.summary: Replaced general rational Sturm allocation on the hot path with an exactly equivalent cubic endpoint/derivative criterion, retained the old Sturm implementation as a differential oracle, and added a source-transparent packed exact candidate scanner. Unfiltered enumeration uses the compiled scanner only after input validation and respects both public resource limits; filtered completion keeps its bounded dynamic stream. Dense CPython and compiled Sage.js tests cover arbitrary coefficients, residue scans, endpoint/repeated roots, resource limits, and GMP promotion. The native benchmark is 102x-303x faster than the old Sturm scan at p=101..10007 and completes the p=1000003 residue class in about 0.20 seconds on the development x64 host.
risks: The integration lane must register the new kernel for production precompilation; without an artifact Sage.js uses the correct optimized dynamic fallback.
Tests and the benchmark live beside the claimed implementation because the hyperelliptic lane cannot claim repository-wide test/bench paths; integration may relocate them.
Packed IntegerBuffer materialization dominates the largest tested row, so a future streaming certificate interface may outperform exhaustive candidate materialization.
next_steps: Register genus3_candidate_kernel.py in the production native-kernel build and witness inventories.
Move or wrap the in-package differential and benchmark drivers in the central test and benchmark manifests.
Run the same compiled stream on Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and native Windows x64 during integration.
